basis: Model-free, source- or metadata-grounded tests applied to whole corpora (not samples), 2026-10-21. They do not replace the human fidelity read; they bound defect classes independently of any LLM judge.

Q2_direction_without_comparison_cue.test: direction in {elevated, depleted/reduced, no significant difference, dysregulated} AND provenance_quote contains no comparison/quantity cue (vs, than, compared, higher/lower, increase/decrease, significant, p<, correlat/associat, %, rate, ...)
Q2_direction_without_comparison_cue.reading: an UPPER BOUND on 'direction asserted without stated comparison' — the regex misses cues like 'indistinguishable' or 'no difference'; use as a sampling stratum, not a verdict; agreement with judge Q2 flags was 1/4 (EDS), 0/3 (POTS)

Q4_tier_vs_publication_type.test: Europe PMC pubType metadata vs evidence_tier: case-report paper with a cohort/RCT/case-control/cross-sectional/meta tier; meta-analysis/systematic-review paper with a case tier; RCT paper with case/review tier
Q4_tier_vs_publication_type.reading: metadata-authoritative; ~1% of rows in both corpora carry an evidence tier incompatible with the paper's indexed publication type; 'meta paper, case tier' may be legitimate (a review quoting a case) and needs a reader. Judge Q4 flags were on papers the metadata test cannot adjudicate (research articles).

Q6_numbers_in_source.test: multi-digit numeric tokens in quantitative_detail located in the retained source text (normalize both sides)
Q6_numbers_in_source.reading: 'all in source, not all in quote' (EDS 854, 13%) is narrow quoting, not fabrication; 'none in source' (EDS 145, 2.2%) is an upper bound inflated by tokenization ('1/5,000', '2 of 15')
